placements.title: From claimed to reference-verified instrument state
placements.frame: What does it mean to anchor an instrument's operational state to an external reference standard rather than to the operator's word alone?

placements.title: Authority shifts from the speaker to the reference standard
placements.frame: When a calibration claim is anchored to a named reference standard, what does the invocation of that standard perform — and what would the claim lose without it?
placements.why: Both expressions assert that the Kestrelwood spectrograph calibration at 88.4 MHz was verified against the June reference plates. The shared theme is the anchoring of authority to an external reference standard rather than to rank or role — a statement true beyond the specific 88.4 MHz measurement, one future envelopes could feed with other reference-verified calibrations.

placements.title: Formatting performs the settling that argument does not
placements.frame: How does bolded label-and-value formatting under a 'Key decisions' header perform ratification of outcomes without deliberation or justification?
placements.why: src-2 labels what follows as 'Key decisions,' performing ratification through the header itself. src-3 and src-4 adopt bolded label-and-value formatting under that header, enacting settled instrument and calibration choices through structural placement rather than through argument. This theme — formatting as a ratification act — is true beyond the specific decisions recorded here.
